title: DS C Rete — architecture
preamble:
# DS C Rete — architecture

Prefix `IRET`.

The design of a purpose-built Rete network
implementation in C that targets only the features DS
uses. This is **not** a general-purpose production-system
engine; every design decision is constrained by the DS
feature set and the DS workload profile (tens to hundreds
of rules, 100–1000 live facts per engine instance).

The implementation lives at `runtime/src/libds/rete/` and is the sole
rule-evaluation engine.
The compiled network travels in the DSC artefact as the
RETP atom set — the `AlphaNode` / `BetaNode` / `TerminalNode` atoms,
which carry their own expression and action trees; the
loader assembles the in-memory node graph from them at
init time.

## What this is not

- Not a general-purpose production-system engine. No module
  system, no object/instance facts, no scripting or runtime
  rule-definition surface.
- Not a compiler. Expression trees and network topology
  arrive pre-compiled in the RETP atom set; the runtime
  assembles the in-memory graph from that description.
- Not a wire-format spec. The RETP atom encodings live in
  [RDSC]
  (the `AlphaNode` / `BetaNode` / `TerminalNode` atoms).
